_comment: Encoded design factors: what a descriptor value implies for making. Edit here, not in code.
_status: PROVISIONAL. Drawn from Study 1 site experience and general handling/fabrication practice. Not verified with domain experts. Every derived output carries data_status 'proposed'.
_circularity_note: Thresholds were informed by Study 1. Agreement between derived outputs and Study 1 decisions is therefore expected and is NOT validation.

handling_class.basis: Manual-handling guidance for single and team lifts; Study 1 site practice.

rules.note: single-person lift
team lift, short carry
machine handling required

handling_class.max_dim_note: Above this longest dimension, a fragment is machine-handled regardless of mass (awkward to grip, unsafe to carry).

connection_strategy.basis: Study 1 timber-to-concrete connections. The classes correspond to those found in the reuse literature: dry mechanical/demountable, post-tensioned, wet/cast, and bearing/interleaving without direct connection [lit. review 5.3]. This factor answers whether a fixing can be SEATED on the face (flatness, area). Whether it can be DRILLED is a separate question, see drill_zone.

rules.note: face not captured by the scan; geometry unverified
flat, large enough to seat a fixing plate
moderately flat; bracket absorbs tolerance
too rough or too small for a fixing

design_assignment.basis: Study 1 spolia principle: cast and finished faces exposed, fracture faces seated or buried.

rules.note: ground-contact face, not observed
carries visible material history: a cast face, adhering tile, or brick cast into the concrete
flat fracture face, suitable for bearing
no rule applies

use_suggestions.basis: Study 1 programme: landscape installation and urban furniture. Fragments serve as supports, stands, shelves, seats and worktops within an assembly. Ground surfacing and downcycling to fill or aggregate are out of scope by design.
use_suggestions._how_to_read: Each entry combines conditions on one face with conditions on the whole fragment. A suggestion is offered when the fragment satisfies requires_fragment and at least one face satisfies requires_face; requires_no_face fires when no face qualifies. Thickness = smallest bounding dimension; aspect ratio = longest / smallest; height_band_mm matches if ANY bounding dimension falls in the band, since the fragment can be laid to present that dimension as height. Which orientation is stable is not computed.

rules.note: flat, smooth cast face large enough to sit at or place objects on; thick enough to span

rules.label: Leaning or backrest surface

rules.note: a face whose material history is legible: formwork marks, adhering tile, or cast-in brick. Condition (weathering, staining) is now reported as a localized anomaly rather than a surface label.

finishing_requirement.basis: Study 1 site practice for a public installation, and general public-realm safety practice. NOT supported by the reuse literature reviewed: that corpus covers cutting, lifting and reconnection, and records surface treatment only once (waterproofing and railings on the Re:Crete footbridge). Treat these as project-derived until evidenced.
finishing_requirement._evidence_gap: No reviewed source specifies treatment of exposed reinforcement, sharp arrises or residual fixings on reused fragments. Kuepfer et al. inspect sawed rebar on cut faces but do not state a treatment. This is a gap worth naming in the paper. Added 2026-08-19: spalling and biological_growth, both from the anomaly axis. Spalling is the one with a real consequence beyond appearance, since it means section loss and probable steel behind, so it bears on whether a face can carry load at all.

rules.note: exposed reinforcement: cut back below the surface, seal against corrosion, remove any protruding end that could injure

adhered tile finish. Two states, and they need different work: whole or fragmentary TILE has to be lifted off, while the bare ADHESIVE BED left where tiles have already come away has to be ground back or keyed. The combed ridges from the notched trowel are the bed, not a concrete finish. The classifier does not separate the two states, so both are named here and which applies must be read off the face. Either way the concrete below is sound and this is a surface layer, not section loss.
rules._provenance: Project-derived from site practice, as with the other entries here: the reuse literature reviewed covers cutting, lifting and reconnection but not surface treatment. Recorded 2026-08-20 from Muchen's identification of the combed adhesive bed on FS-004.

rules.note: rough break with sharp edges: ease arrises on any face within reach in public use
moss, algae or lichen: this was a weather face. Clean before handling or exposing, and expect it to return if the face is re-exposed
exposed face: clean; sealing optional and changes appearance
ground-contact face, not exposed in use
no treatment indicated

drill_zone.basis: Reinforcement in a slab is a mat of bars at roughly constant cover and spacing, so most of the section is steel-free and the question is where to drill, not whether. Cover and spacing are not measured here; the values below are conservative assumptions for mid-twentieth-century slabs, where cover is often below current code minima. GPR is the established verification before cutting or drilling [Kuepfer et al.].
drill_zone._evidence_gap: Bar positions are not yet extracted from the scan. Where reinforcement is visible on a fracture face, that face is a section through the mat and its spacing, direction and cover are in principle measurable from the localized anomaly. Not implemented.

rules.note: reinforcement is exposed somewhere on the fragment, so the mat's spacing, direction and cover can be read off it and projected across the piece; a hole set out in the middle of a grid opening passes the mat without striking steel
no bars visible, but the section is deep enough for a steel-free core between the two mats; a hole entering the broken edge at mid-thickness runs parallel to and clear of both
bar layout unobservable and the section too thin for a reliable steel-free core; scan before drilling, or fix without drilling

_taxonomy_note: 2026-08-19: original_finish, weathered and staining were retired as SURFACE labels. weathered and staining remain ANOMALY labels, which is a different axis: an anomaly is localized and carries a bounding box, so condition is now reported as a patch on a face rather than as the identity of the face. Rules using `if_anomaly` are unaffected; only `labels` and `if_label` lists were updated. See 04_schema/TAXONOMY_REVIEW.md.
